Requirement: Excluded from the Act.

Requirement: Excluded from the Act.

Requirement: Determine role per processing activity.
Current-state diagnostic question: For each processing activity, are you the Data Fiduciary (determine purpose & means), a Data Processor (process on another's behalf), or both?

Requirement: Maintain a processing inventory mapping each activity to its lawful ground.
Current-state diagnostic question: Is every processing activity for a lawful purpose (not expressly forbidden by law) and grounded in either consent (§6) or a certain legitimate use (§7)?

Requirement: Scope out exempt processing with the specific clause recorded.
Current-state diagnostic question: Does any processing fall under a §17 exemption (legal claims; courts/regulatory bodies; offence prevention/investigation; non-India principals under a foreign contract; M&A/insolvency; loan-default financial assessment; notified State instrumentalities; research/archiving/statistical per Rules Second Schedule)?

Requirement: Conditional exemption from §5, §8(3), §8(7), §10 and §11.
Current-state diagnostic question: Are you a startup or other class notified by the Central Government as exempt from §5, §8(3), §8(7), §10 and §11?

Requirement: Every consent request is accompanied or preceded by a notice stating (i) the personal data and purpose, (ii) how to exercise rights under §6(4) and §13, and (iii) how to complain to the Board.
Current-state diagnostic question: Is a compliant notice presented at or before every point consent is collected?

Requirement: The notice is understandable independently of any other information the Data Fiduciary makes available.
Current-state diagnostic question: Is the notice a standalone, self-contained document (not buried in a longer T&C)?

Requirement: In clear, plain language the notice gives, at minimum, (i) an itemised description of the personal data, and (ii) the specified purpose(s) plus a specific description of the goods/services/uses enabled.
Current-state diagnostic question: Does each notice itemise the exact data fields and tie them to specific purposes?

Requirement: The notice gives the communication link (website/app) and other means to withdraw consent (ease comparable to giving it), exercise rights, and complain to the Board.
Current-state diagnostic question: Are working links/means for withdrawal, rights and Board complaints present in every notice?

Requirement: For consent obtained before commencement, a notice (data + purpose processed; how to exercise rights under §6(4)/§13; how to complain to the Board) is given as soon as reasonably practicable; processing may continue until consent is withdrawn.
Current-state diagnostic question: Has a back-notice been issued (or planned) for all pre-existing consented data?

Requirement: The principal can access the notice in English or any language in the Eighth Schedule to the Constitution.
Current-state diagnostic question: Is the notice available in English and the relevant Eighth-Schedule language(s)?

Requirement: Consent is free, specific, informed, unconditional and unambiguous, given by a clear affirmative action, and limited to the personal data necessary for the specified purpose.
Current-state diagnostic question: Is consent captured by affirmative action, unbundled, and limited to necessary data (no pre-ticked boxes, no bundling unnecessary data)?

Requirement: Any part of consent that infringes the Act/Rules or other law is invalid to that extent.
Current-state diagnostic question: Are consent texts reviewed so no clause waives statutory rights (e.g. right to complain)?

Requirement: Consent requests are in clear and plain language, with a language option (English / Eighth Schedule), and include the contact details of the DPO (where applicable) or other authorised person for rights queries.
Current-state diagnostic question: Do consent requests carry plain-language text, language choice, and a contact for rights queries?

Requirement: The principal can withdraw consent at any time, with ease comparable to giving it; withdrawal consequences are borne by the principal and do not affect the legality of prior processing.
Current-state diagnostic question: Is there a withdrawal mechanism as easy as the opt-in?

Requirement: On withdrawal, the Data Fiduciary ceases - and causes its processors to cease - processing within a reasonable time, unless otherwise required/authorised by law.
Current-state diagnostic question: On withdrawal, does processing (yours and your processors') actually stop within a reasonable time?

Requirement: The principal may give/manage/review/withdraw consent through a Consent Manager.
Current-state diagnostic question: Is consent-via-Consent-Manager supported (or a documented decision not to, pending the ecosystem)?

Requirement: The Data Fiduciary must be able to prove, in a proceeding, that notice was given and valid consent obtained.
Current-state diagnostic question: Are immutable, auditable consent + notice records retained per data subject and purpose?

Conditional: Conditional - only if registering/acting as a Consent Manager (rule 4 commences ~13 Nov 2026)
Requirement: Registered with the Board; applicant is a company incorporated in India with net worth >= Rs 2 crore, sound finances/management, and independent certification of an interoperable, standards-compliant consent platform.
Current-state diagnostic question: Do you meet and evidence every Part A registration condition?

Conditional: Conditional - only if registering/acting as a Consent Manager (rule 4 commences ~13 Nov 2026)
Requirement: The consent/sharing mechanism is such that contents are not readable by the Consent Manager.
Current-state diagnostic question: Is the platform architected so the CM cannot read the data it routes?

Conditional: Conditional - only if registering/acting as a Consent Manager (rule 4 commences ~13 Nov 2026)
Requirement: Maintain a record of consents given/denied/withdrawn, notices, and sharing; give the principal access and machine-readable copies; retain >= 7 years.
Current-state diagnostic question: Are consent records kept, accessible, and retained for at least seven years?

Conditional: Conditional - only if registering/acting as a Consent Manager (rule 4 commences ~13 Nov 2026)
Requirement: No sub-contracting; act in a fiduciary capacity; avoid conflicts of interest with Data Fiduciaries (directors/KMP/ownership).
Current-state diagnostic question: Are no-subcontracting and conflict-of-interest controls in place?

Conditional: Conditional - only if registering/acting as a Consent Manager (rule 4 commences ~13 Nov 2026)
Requirement: Take reasonable security safeguards; publish ownership/management transparency info; maintain audit mechanisms reporting to the Board; no change of control without Board approval.
Current-state diagnostic question: Are safeguards, transparency disclosures, audits and control-change approvals operating?

Requirement: For data the principal voluntarily provided for a specified purpose and has not objected to: process only for that purpose, and cease when she indicates she no longer wants it.
Current-state diagnostic question: Where you rely on voluntary provision, is the purpose documented and an objection/stop path honoured?

Requirement: State subsidy/benefit/service/certificate/licence/permit processing follows the Second Schedule standards (lawful, purpose-limited, accurate, secured, intimation + contact + rights link given).
Current-state diagnostic question: If relying on §7(b), are the Second-Schedule standards met?

Requirement: Processing for State legal functions / sovereignty & security, legal disclosure obligations, or court judgments/orders is confined to those grounds.
Current-state diagnostic question: Are any of these grounds relied on, and documented per activity?

Requirement: Processing for medical emergency, epidemic/public-health measures, or disaster/breakdown of public order is confined to those grounds.
Current-state diagnostic question: Are emergency/public-health/disaster grounds relied on, and scoped?

Requirement: Employment-purpose processing (or to safeguard the employer from loss/liability - e.g. trade-secret/IP confidentiality, services/benefits to an employee) is confined to that ground.
Current-state diagnostic question: For employee data, is the §7(i) basis recorded and limited to employment purposes?

Section: 4. General obligations of a Data Fiduciary
Requirement: The Data Fiduciary is responsible for compliance for all processing by it or by a Data Processor on its behalf, irrespective of any contrary agreement or the principal's failure of duties.
Current-state diagnostic question: Is accountability for processor processing owned and evidenced (not contracted away)?

Section: 4. General obligations of a Data Fiduciary
Requirement: A Data Processor is engaged only under a valid contract, which requires reasonable security safeguards.
Current-state diagnostic question: Is there a valid, safeguards-bearing contract with every processor?

Section: 4. General obligations of a Data Fiduciary
Requirement: Where data is used to make a decision affecting the principal or disclosed to another Data Fiduciary, ensure its completeness, accuracy and consistency.
Current-state diagnostic question: Are accuracy controls applied before decisions/disclosures?

Section: 4. General obligations of a Data Fiduciary
Requirement: Implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure effective observance of the Act/Rules.
Current-state diagnostic question: Are TOMs designed, documented and operating across the data lifecycle?

Section: 4. General obligations of a Data Fiduciary
Requirement: Take reasonable security safeguards to prevent breach, at minimum: (a) encryption/obfuscation/masking/tokenisation; (b) access control to computer resources; (c) logging, monitoring and review for unauthorised-access detection; (d) backups for continued processing; (e) retain logs and personal data for 1 year; (f) safeguards clauses in processor contracts; (g) supporting technical & organisational measures.
Current-state diagnostic question: Are all seven Rule-6 minimum safeguards in place and evidenced (incl. >= 1-year log retention)?

Section: 4. General obligations of a Data Fiduciary
Requirement: On becoming aware of a breach, intimate each affected Data Principal without delay via her user account/registered channel, stating: nature/extent/timing, likely consequences to her, mitigation measures, safety steps she can take, and a contact.
Current-state diagnostic question: Is there a tested process to notify affected principals without delay with all five content elements?

Section: 4. General obligations of a Data Fiduciary
Requirement: Intimate the Board without delay (nature, extent, timing, location, likely impact) and within 72 hours (or a longer Board-allowed period) give: updated description, facts/circumstances/reasons, mitigation, findings on who caused it, recurrence-prevention measures, and a report on principal-intimations.
Current-state diagnostic question: Is there a 72-hour Board-notification playbook with all six follow-up elements?

Section: 4. General obligations of a Data Fiduciary
Requirement: Erase personal data on consent withdrawal, or when it is reasonable to assume the specified purpose is no longer served - whichever is earlier - unless retention is required by law.
Current-state diagnostic question: Are deletion triggers (withdrawal / purpose-end) implemented with a legal-hold exception?

Section: 4. General obligations of a Data Fiduciary
Requirement: Cause your Data Processor to erase any personal data you made available to it.
Current-state diagnostic question: Do processor contracts/runbooks force downstream erasure on the same triggers?

Section: 4. General obligations of a Data Fiduciary
Conditional: Applies to Third-Schedule classes; else N/A
Requirement: Apply the no-longer-served time period for erasure. For the notified classes (e-commerce >= 2 cr users; online gaming >= 50 lakh users; social media >= 2 cr users) the period is 3 years from the principal's last engagement (or Rules' commencement, whichever later). Notify the principal >= 48 hours before erasure.
Current-state diagnostic question: If in a Third-Schedule class, is the 3-year clock + 48-hour pre-erasure notice implemented? (Else record N/A.)

Section: 4. General obligations of a Data Fiduciary
Requirement: Retain personal data, traffic data and logs for >= 1 year for the Seventh-Schedule purposes, then erase, unless another law requires longer.
Current-state diagnostic question: Is the >= 1-year retention-then-erase rule applied to data/traffic/logs?

Section: 4. General obligations of a Data Fiduciary
Requirement: Prominently publish on website/app, and state in every rights-response, the business contact of the DPO (if applicable) or a person who can answer the principal's processing questions.
Current-state diagnostic question: Is the answerable-person contact published prominently and echoed in every rights response?

Section: 4. General obligations of a Data Fiduciary
Requirement: Establish an effective grievance-redressal mechanism; publish it; respond within the published period (not exceeding 90 days) and maintain TOMs ensuring effectiveness.
Current-state diagnostic question: Is a published grievance mechanism live with a defined SLA <= 90 days and effectiveness controls?

Requirement: Before processing a child's (under-18) data, obtain verifiable parental consent: adopt TOMs and due diligence that the self-identified parent is an identifiable adult - via reliable details already held, voluntarily provided identity/age, a virtual token from an authorised entity, or a DigiLocker provider.
Current-state diagnostic question: Is a verifiable-parental-consent + adult-verification flow implemented for child data?

Requirement: For a person with disability with a lawful guardian, obtain verifiable guardian consent, with due diligence that the guardian was appointed by a court / designated authority / local-level committee under the applicable guardianship law.
Current-state diagnostic question: Is guardian-appointment verification implemented for this population?

Requirement: Do not undertake processing likely to cause a detrimental effect on a child's well-being.
Current-state diagnostic question: Is there a safeguard/assessment preventing detrimental-effect processing of children?

Requirement: Do not undertake tracking, behavioural monitoring of children, or targeted advertising directed at children.
Current-state diagnostic question: Are child tracking / behavioural monitoring / targeted ads disabled?

Requirement: Reliance on an exemption from §9(1)/(3) is confined to a notified class (e.g. clinical/mental-health/healthcare, educational institutions, creches/child-care, school transport) or purpose (Part B), within the stated conditions.
Current-state diagnostic question: If exempt processing is relied on, is the exact Fourth-Schedule class/purpose + condition documented?
